experiences.title: Coalesce edits per document and restart the quiet interval
experiences.applicability: The task explicitly requires reusing an existing trailing utility to retain the latest text in an editing burst until a quiet interval expires.
experiences.event_relation: Replace pending text and restart the timer on every edit. Save only the latest value at expiration, and allow later independent bursts to save again. Use separate tasks for different documents.
experiences.preservation: Preserve existing interfaces and exact input, including empty strings. Preserve the guard that prevents writes when there is no current document.
experiences.exclusion: The historical editor cases use 120 ms; this is not a universal constant. Do not discard intermediate values when the task requires processing every event.
experiences.verification: With a controlled clock, check no early write, deadline restart after another edit, one latest-value write at expiration, a successful second burst, empty text and independent document tasks.

experiences.title: Consume batch state before invoking the save callback
experiences.applicability: A reusable task invokes its save callback synchronously, and that callback may edit again or flush the task.
experiences.event_relation: Capture the value to consume, clear that batch's timer and pending state, and then invoke saving. Edits created by synchronous callbacks belong to the next batch.
experiences.preservation: Preserve later reuse, avoid consuming the old value twice, and do not erase callback-created work during outer cleanup. Retain the existing absence sentinel.
experiences.exclusion: Do not make saving a terminal state. Do not replace None/null/nil checks with truthiness checks that discard valid empty strings.
experiences.verification: Edit again and invoke a nested flush inside the save callback. Check that the old batch saves once, the new batch remains pending and it completes at its next deadline.

experiences.title: Clean up document buffers and view subscriptions separately
experiences.applicability: A store, BufferBank or coordinator dictionary owns persistent document buffers; the view owns only its current status subscription.
experiences.event_relation: On departure, clean up the subscription captured by that view without discarding pending document text or destroying a document task that must remain reusable. Reopening locates its buffer by document identity.
experiences.preservation: Preserve isolation between documents, same-document reopening, status unsubscription and continuing persistence responsibility. Determine the actual owner from the current implementation.
experiences.exclusion: View detachment does not imply cancellation of persistent work. Persistent ownership alone also does not require immediate departure flushing.
experiences.verification: Switch, close, dispose and reopen the same document with pending text. Check buffer reuse, subscription release and eventual persistence to the original document separately.

experiences.title: Bind deferred writes to the document that accepted the edit
experiences.applicability: Text is accepted before its write occurs, and the current view may change in between.
experiences.event_relation: Bind the task and save closure to the document or buffer key that accepted the edit, rather than looking up the current view when the timer executes.
experiences.preservation: Preserve document IDs, original text, empty text and the no-current-view edit guard. Status events retain store-generated semantics.
experiences.exclusion: Do not write a departing document's text into the new document or merge pending slots for different documents merely to reuse a task.
experiences.verification: Edit A, switch to B and then fire A's timer to check write ownership. Interleave edits to two documents, clear text and attempt editing after closure.

summary.text: Applies to document saving where edits are accepted before deferred writes and the current view may switch or close in between. Bind pending tasks and save closures to the document or buffer key that accepted the edit. Timer callbacks must not choose the write target by reading the current view. Preserve the original document identity, exact text including empty text, the guard rejecting edits without a current view, and storage-generated status semantics. Do not merge different documents' pending slots merely to reuse a task. Check editing then switching before the old timer fires, interleaved edits to two documents, clearing text and edits after close; old content must always return to its original document.

experiences.title: Distinguish retained persistence responsibility from a departure deadline
experiences.applicability: Historical guidance contains two boundary interpretations: completion before departure inferred from original synchronous writes and preservation, and buffer survival with the deadline requiring separate support.
experiences.event_relation: Establish the current task's boundary semantics first. If completion before open/close/dispose or submission returns is explicitly required, flush the captured original document and consume its timer. If only retention is required, continue scheduling under that contract.
experiences.preservation: Neither branch may silently lose accepted text. An explicit deadline also requires preventing a later duplicate save.
experiences.exclusion: A synchronous API, persistent ownership, generic preservation wording or one passing test alone does not establish a before-return deadline. A later version's wording must not automatically overwrite an older branch that has supporting evidence.
experiences.verification: For an explicit deadline, read storage immediately after return and advance the clock to check for duplicates. For retention, check that work remains owned by the original document and completes at the specified time.

summary.text: Applies when deferred saving encounters open, close, destruction or submission boundaries and retained work must be distinguished from a deadline before return. Establish boundary semantics from the current task and source. If completion before return is explicitly required, settle the captured original document and consume its scheduled execution to prevent duplicate saving. If only retention is required, continue under its scheduling contract. Neither branch may lose accepted text. Synchronous APIs, durable ownership, generic retention wording or a single passing check do not independently establish a before-return deadline. Wording in later versions must not overwrite a supported older branch. For deadline contracts, check storage at return and later duplication; otherwise check original-document ownership and the agreed completion schedule.

experiences.title: Prevent departure cleanup and rendering from overwriting callback navigation
experiences.applicability: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.
experiences.event_relation: Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
experiences.preservation: Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
experiences.exclusion: Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.
experiences.verification: Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

summary.text: Applies to editors where saving or subscription cleanup synchronously invokes host listeners that may open documents or close the workspace. Capture the old view and revoke its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects such as clearing before callback-capable saving, or recheck authority for remaining effects after callbacks. Outer open operations must recheck request identity after retiring the old view. Preserve nested navigation, nested edits and new-view rendering; destruction cleans only captured old resources. Guarding final view installation alone does not prevent late clearing. Nor is detaching first a universal order for every host. Check navigation reentry, subscriptions and nested edits during timer saves, departure saves and actual unmount.

experiences.title: Preserve entry text and returned results for accepted submissions
experiences.applicability: Submission accepts a document and text at entry, and its contract requires that accepted text to become durable before recording the result.
experiences.event_relation: Capture the document and text at submission entry. Complete the required save before recording and returning that submission's result. Navigation inside save or record callbacks must not rewrite the accepted submission.
experiences.preservation: Retain the durable result and return value bound to entry. Edits after callbacks form new work and must not be consumed by the earlier submission.
experiences.exclusion: Do not transfer this retention policy to tasks where navigation may revoke submission. Do not substitute the latest current text for the result bound to entry text.
experiences.verification: Navigate and edit inside save and record callbacks. Separately check the entry document's saved value, submission record, synchronous return value and successful persistence of later edits.

experiences.title: Show submission confirmation only for the accepting visit
experiences.applicability: A durable submission result may survive navigation, but visible confirmation belongs only to the visit that accepted the operation.
experiences.event_relation: Before showing confirmation, check that the originating visit is still current. When closure, replacement or same-document reopening creates a distinct visit, old confirmation must not revive.
experiences.preservation: Keep durable submission results and return values under the acceptance contract. Loss of display permission does not justify discarding the result.
experiences.exclusion: Equal document IDs do not establish equal visit identity. Do not combine confirmation visibility, persistence and result recording into one gate.
experiences.verification: Switch, close and reopen the same document inside submission callbacks. Check that the durable result remains, old confirmation disappears and legitimate current confirmation still works.

summary.text: Applies when submission results must persist but visible confirmation belongs only to the visit that accepted the operation. Before showing confirmation, check that the original visit is still current. Closing, replacing or reopening the same document creates a new visit, after which old confirmation must not reappear. Preserve persistent submission results and return values under the acceptance contract. Separate result recording, persistence and confirmation authority; losing display eligibility must not discard the result. Equal document identifiers do not imply equal visit identity. Check switching, closing and reopening the same document from submission callbacks: results remain, old confirmation disappears, and valid current confirmation is not disabled.

experiences.title: Order save notifications according to the current host contract
experiences.applicability: View subscriptions define document filtering, event payloads and retirement notifications. Historical cases include both removal before saving and preserving a departing view's opportunity to receive its save status.
experiences.event_relation: Preserve document reads and presentation, original event payloads and filtering. If the host requires the departing view to receive this save notification, deliver it in that order before removal. If retirement immediately forbids UI effects, mark invalidity first and protect later output.
experiences.preservation: Preserve public and injected interfaces, exact text, store-generated status and revision semantics, and normal subscription release.
experiences.exclusion: Do not force different cases' notification contracts into one cleanup order. Checking stored values alone can miss status-display regressions and subscription leaks.
experiences.verification: Observe notification-versus-detachment order, events after retirement, filtering of other documents, reads on reopening, and document/status output after nested navigation.

summary.text: Applies to document saves whose view subscriptions specify document filtering, event payloads and retirement-notification order. Hosts may require detachment before saving or require the departing view to receive its save status. Follow the current notification contract: deliver required departure-save notifications before removal; if retirement ends UI authority, mark the visit invalid first and guard subsequent output. Preserve document reads and presentation, exact text, storage-generated status and revision semantics, public and injected interfaces, and normal subscription release. Do not collapse different contracts into one cleanup order. Check notification/removal order, post-retirement events, filtering of other documents, reads after reopening, and document and status output after navigation reentry. Storage-value checks alone are insufficient.

experiences.title: Preserve discard-on-hide and reuse for transient previews
experiences.applicability: Persistent editor saving and search preview share a trailing utility, but preview has its own lifetime and cancellation policy.
experiences.event_relation: Retain the preview's quiet interval, cancellation of unpublished work on hide and normal scheduling of subsequent queries. Verify preview behavior when changing the shared utility.
experiences.preservation: Historical cases use 40 ms for preview and 120 ms for the editor. Preserve each case's parameters without treating them as defaults for new tasks.
experiences.exclusion: Do not turn preview hide into document departure flushing or apply preview's discard policy to persistent document work.
experiences.verification: Hide before the preview deadline and check no output, then issue another query and check normal output. Interleave pending editor work and verify independent parameters and lifetimes.

summary.text: Applies when persistent editing and search previews share a trailing-edge delay helper but differ in lifecycle and cancellation policy. Preserve the preview's own quiet interval, cancellation of unpublished work on hide and ability to schedule future queries. Verify previews independently when changing the shared helper. The original 40 ms preview and 120 ms editor intervals are case-specific parameters, not defaults for new tasks. Do not replace hidden-preview discard with document-departure settlement or apply preview discard to durable document work. Check that hiding before the deadline prevents output, a later query can still publish, and interleaved preview and pending-save work retain independent timing and lifecycles.

experiences.title: Verify cleanup and exposed interfaces through the actual component entry
experiences.applicability: A framework component or workspace wrapper exposes the coordinator. Correct direct calls do not establish correct component unmounting.
experiences.event_relation: Follow the current integration's actual call path for dispose, subscription removal and navigation ownership. Do not import lifecycle behavior from another framework version.
experiences.preservation: Preserve the interfaces actually present: React effect cleanup, Vue 2 beforeDestroy, Vue 3 onBeforeUnmount/expose, jQuery events or the corresponding native entry points.
experiences.exclusion: These are alternatives from different cases, not requirements for one project to implement together. A native embedding does not imply a DOM or Promise runtime.
experiences.verification: Check both public coordinator calls and actual component unmounting. Navigate inside an unmount-triggered save and check the new view, externally callable APIs and resource release.

summary.text: Applies when a framework component or workspace wrapper exposes a coordinator and unmount or cleanup may synchronously reenter navigation. Correct direct coordinator calls do not replace verification through the actual component-unmount path. Follow the dispose, subscription-removal and navigation-ownership chain present in the current integration. Preserve existing React effect cleanup, Vue 2 beforeDestroy, Vue 3 onBeforeUnmount and expose, jQuery events or native entry points, rather than transplanting another framework version's lifecycle. These interfaces are alternatives for different settings; native embedding does not necessarily provide DOM or Promise runtimes. Check nested navigation, new views, externally callable interfaces and resource release when unmount triggers saving.
